original_test_intent: Verify a designated member removal from an approved disposable NVMe RAID1 creates the documented degraded/fail condition and physical RAID-fail LED.
original_method: After critical approval, a qualified operator creates/handles the exact disposable array and removes one mapped member while the agent records controller, member, LED, OS/BMC and recovery evidence.
manual_activity: Engineer resolves scope and authorizes destructive disposable-array steps; qualified operator creates/records the array, removes only the mapped member and observes the LED.
required_inputs: Decision on SAS/SATA identity versus literal NVMe RAID-fail scope
Platform fail-LED state/timing and supported controller fault semantics
Two disposable SSD serials with member/controller/enclosure/slot mapping
Approved RAID1 create/init, member-removal, degraded hold and recovery procedure
Qualified operator, maintenance window, OOB, backup and protected evidence
safety_requirements: Use only verified disposable non-boot non-management media
Capture healthy array and confirm no rebuild/background task before removal
Remove exactly one mapped member and stop on wrong slot, uncontrolled rebuild, data/filesystem/thermal/power/BMC fault or recovery loss
Keep recovery a separate explicit authorization
Do not force online, clear faults, use raw IPMI or remove a second member
agent_execution_scope: Record complete array create/init and healthy baseline
Monitor exact physical/virtual member, degraded, rebuild, health and logs
Correlate operator removal and LED observation timestamps
Do not choose media, handle hardware, authorize recovery or issue verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve scope and approve destructive targets, fail matrix and recovery
Provide qualified operator and own array/data recovery
Review transition evidence and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Locate/raw LED control is not a RAID failure stimulus and lsblk cannot prove controller-degraded membership or data safety.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the pinned vendor RAID interface to create/verify the isolated RAID1, monitor exact member removal and degraded state, paired with physical LED evidence; recover only under separate approval.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NVMe RAID1 creation, one-member unplug, fail-LED inspection and source 15/8 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat create, healthy baseline, one-member removal, degraded observation and recovery disposition as separately evidenced phases with stable identities.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds destructive consent, exact membership, controller-state proof and recovery control without weakening the failure stimulus.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Automation monitors array state; physical removal and LED observation remain manual.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Array creation can erase both drives and removal may immediately start controller-specific rebuild or failover behavior.

project_override_considerations: The project must resolve SAS/SATA versus NVMe scope and approve the exact controller's RAID1 semantics; no generic indicator command or production array may be used.
expected_evidence: Scope decision, critical approval and platform fail-LED matrix
RAID1 create/init output and healthy baseline
Operator identity, removal timestamp and physical LED evidence
Controller degraded/member/rebuild state plus OS/health/temperature/SEL logs
Approved degraded or recovered disposition and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: SAS/SATA grouping conflicts with an explicit NVMe RAID1 creation and NVMe member-removal procedure; authoritative device-family scope requires engineering decision.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Execution remains pending critical approval, disposable targets and recovery plan, but static review is complete and the review queue may continue.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Compatibility row115 Wistron-Storage-00098-V003: decide whether the authoritative destructive case is NVMe RAID1 fail despite SAS/SATA grouping, a SAS/SATA RAID-fail case, or separate variants; provide exact disposable members/slot/controller map, fail-LED timing, supported create/remove/degraded procedure, abort limits and separately approved recovery. Locate/raw IPMI must not substitute for real degraded state.

review_improvement: Restores the real destructive RAID failure transition, exposes the hardware-scope conflict and prevents indicator-only evidence from hiding array/data risk.
independent_technical_reasoning: A fail LED is meaningful only when tied to an independently proven controller member state. Removing a drive can degrade the array, start rebuild, or affect the wrong virtual disk, so stable serial/member mapping and controller telemetry must bracket the physical removal; an LED command alone has no evidentiary link to RAID failure.
